Parse the secondary-unit line into a comparable identifier

Source: R/unit.R
pf_parse_unit.Rd

Extracts the unit from a raw PF_15_G_PAID_RECIP_ADDR_L2 value and returns it as type plus id, or "" for both when the line does not hold a unit.

Usage

pf_parse_unit(x, street = NULL)

Arguments

x

Character vector of raw address line 2 values.

street

Optional street line, same length as x. When it names a PO box, a bare identifier in x is rejected: at a box address the digits on line 2 are a box or account number, not a door. 211 EMMET STREET SOUTH PO BOX with 400891 on line 2 is the case. A value carrying an explicit designator is still read as a unit.

Value

A data frame with type and id, one row per input.

Details

A line is rejected when it is a PO box, when it looks like a street address (a leading house number followed by a street-type word), or when it carries no digits at all — STREET, LAS VEGAS and 114 HIGH ST are all real values of this field.

type separates room-level designators (STE, UNIT, APT, RM, …, normalized to STE) from level-level ones (FL, BLDG, TOWER, …), so that FL 2 is not read as the same place as STE 2. A bare identifier with no designator — 206, A-304 — gets type "", and compares equal to a room-level unit with the same id, since a filer writing Suite 206 and one writing 206 at the same street mean the same door.

See also

pf_unit_evidence()
